observations: State guide explicitly separates player discovery, enabled state, route readiness and suggestion usefulness.
Both guides separate acceptance, response text, committed effects and readiness, and require live executor rechecks.
State guide says requires checks current public fact presence, not value; provider must update guards.
Window examples update enabled gates, preserve unknown lock state, and mark the incidental lick command on_request.
State guide requires branch separation, observation-time ordering and stable entity IDs for cross-room identity.
Passive look is explicitly current supplied description without input or a menu; authored text must be refreshed by the provider.

limits: Provider facts, receipt semantics, input guards, readiness and audience are authored assertions; this review does not independently establish their truth.
No live asynchronous runner, native game, flag extractor, voice frontend, input ownership fence or desktop execution was exercised.
Out-of-order and busy-state checks simulate serialized provider packets; they are not concurrency or live engine timing qualification.
Passive look reads the latest supplied snapshot; it does not refresh a live game or regenerate stale provider prose.
Source and repository tests were intentionally not inspected; engineering-quality verdict is limited to installed public-boundary behavior and guidance.
